subject: psychiatry
title: Illness Anxiety, Factitious Disorder, and Malingering

steps.tx: **Illness anxiety disorder**, historically termed hypochondriasis, is characterized by preoccupation with having or acquiring a serious, undiagnosed medical illness, despite minimal or absent somatic symptoms. If physical sensations are present, they are normal physiological variants, such as harmless borborygmi, interpreted as catastrophic malignant disease.
steps.say: Illness anxiety disorder involves persistent preoccupation with harboring a serious undiagnosed disease, despite minimal or absent somatic symptoms.

left.title: Illness Anxiety Disorder
points: Somatic symptoms absent or very mild
Preoccupation with the idea of being sick
High anxiety regarding medical diagnoses
Excessive checking or complete doctor avoidance

right.title: Somatic Symptom Disorder
points: Prominent, distressing physical symptoms present
Focus is on the distress caused by the pain
Chronic pain, fatigue, and bowel complaints
Seeks medical relief for physical sensations

steps.tx: **Care-seeking versus care-avoidant subtypes** characterize patients with illness anxiety disorder based on their health utilization behaviors. Care-seeking individuals repeatedly schedule medical appointments, consult multiple specialists, and request invasive imaging; care-avoidant individuals avoid doctors and hospitals due to overwhelming terror that lethal cancer will be diagnosed.
steps.say: Illness anxiety divides into care-seeking patients who demand endless scans and care-avoidant patients who fearfully shun all hospitals.

vis.title: Illness Anxiety Behavioral Phenotypes
rows: Frequent clinic visits, doctor shopping, repeat MRIs
Iatrogenic harm from unnecessary invasive procedures
Avoids all medical appointments, clinics, and testing
Delay in diagnosing genuine emergent medical illness
Repeated reassurance provides relief for hours only
Compulsive searching of medical symptom databases
Escalates catastrophic interpretation of normal body signs

steps.tx: Even inside illness anxiety, patients do not all behave the same way at the clinic door. **Care-seeking versus care-avoidant subtypes** divide them by how they use health care. Care seeking people book appointment after appointment, consult many specialists, and request invasive imaging. Care avoidant people stay away from doctors and hospitals because they are overwhelmed by terror that a lethal cancer will be diagnosed. Both are preoccupied with serious disease.
steps.say: Illness anxiety splits into care seeking patients, who repeatedly request specialists and invasive scans, and care avoidant patients, who shun doctors and hospitals for fear a fatal cancer will be found. Both groups are preoccupied with serious illness. The subtype records how they use care, not a different fear.

vis.alt: A four column matrix contrasts illness anxiety disorder, somatic symptom disorder, factitious disorder, and malingering.
vis.caption: Preoccupation with illness, distress from symptoms, deception aimed at the sick role, and deception aimed at an external reward are set in separate columns. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Factitious disorder**, also designated Munchausen syndrome when severe, is characterized by the intentional falsification, fabrication, or self-induction of physical or psychological signs or symptoms. The individual presents themselves as ill, injured, or impaired, with the sole deceptive motive of assuming the sick role.
steps.say: Factitious disorder involves deliberate fabrication or induction of illness to assume the patient role, without external financial incentives.

left.title: Factitious Disorder
points: Deliberate deception and symptom fabrication
Primary psychological motive: sick role adoption
Absence of external financial or legal gain
Willingness to undergo painful invasive surgery

right.title: Malingering Presentation
points: Deliberate exaggeration or feigning of disease
Motivated purely by tangible external incentives
Avoids military duty, prison, or gains money
Refuses painful or risky medical procedures

steps.tx: **Methods of symptom fabrication in factitious disorder** demonstrate remarkable medical sophistication, including contaminating urine samples with feces to simulate sepsis, injecting insulin to induce hypoglycaemia, or manipulating clinical thermometers. Patients frequently possess medical backgrounds, exhibit multiple abdominal laparotomy scars (gridiron abdomen), and wander between hospitals under pseudonyms.
steps.say: Factitious patients fabricate illness by contaminating urine, injecting insulin, or tampering with thermometers, often displaying multiple surgical scars.

vis.title: Common Factitious Mechanisms
rows: Self-injection of saliva or feces into intravenous lines
Polymicrobial blood cultures with oral/fecal flora
Low C-peptide paired with high serum insulin
Adding finger-prick blood to clean urine specimen
Cystoscopy normal; supervised clean-catch specimen clear
Application of caustic chemicals or mechanical scratching
Lesions confined to areas reachable by dominant hand

steps.tx: **Factitious disorder imposed on another**, historically termed Munchausen syndrome by proxy or medical child abuse, involves a perpetrator fabricating or inducing physical illness in another vulnerable person, typically a mother harming her young child. The perpetrator deceptively presents the victim as sick, seeking attention as a devoted caregiver.
steps.say: Factitious disorder imposed on another involves a caregiver fabricating illness in a child to gain attention, constituting severe child abuse.

nodes.label: Child with bizarre, recurrent illness resolving only when mother is absent
Mother appears remarkably calm, medically knowledgeable, and refuses to leave
Implement covert video surveillance or strict supervised nursing separation
Immediate child protection notification and legal separation to prevent fatality

steps.tx: A child can be made to look ill so that a caregiver receives attention. **Factitious disorder imposed on another**, historically Munchausen syndrome by proxy or medical child abuse, is the fabrication or induction of physical illness in a vulnerable person, typically a mother harming her young child. The perpetrator presents the victim as sick and seeks the status of a devoted caregiver. The flowchart forces a separation from genuine paediatric disease and from injuries inflicted as straightforward assault.
steps.say: Factitious disorder imposed on another, once called Munchausen syndrome by proxy, is a caregiver inventing or causing illness in a vulnerable person, usually a mother and her young child. The child is presented as sick so the adult is seen as a devoted carer. It is medical child abuse, not ordinary illness.

vis.alt: A forensic flowchart separates factitious disorder imposed on another from genuine paediatric illness and from intentional physical abuse.
vis.caption: The chart asks whether a caregiver induced or invented the illness, whether the child is truly sick, or whether the injuries are direct assault. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Malingering** is not a mental disorder, but a calculated behavior defined as the intentional production of false or grossly exaggerated physical or psychological symptoms motivated entirely by external incentives. Secondary gains driving malingering include evading military conscription or criminal prosecution, obtaining financial disability compensation, or securing hospital shelter.
steps.say: Malingering is the intentional feigning of illness motivated by external rewards like disability money, dodging criminal charges, or avoiding work.

steps.tx: **Secondary gain versus primary gain** delineates the psychological rewards operating in somatic conditions. Primary gain, characteristic of conversion disorder, refers to the internal reduction of psychological conflict achieved by converting distress into physical symptoms; secondary gain refers to external advantages gained from being sick, such as disability payments.
steps.say: Primary gain resolves internal psychological conflict through somatic conversion. Secondary gain provides external benefits like financial disability payments.

left.title: Primary Gain
points: Internal emotional conflict resolution
Anxiety kept outside conscious awareness
Characteristic of conversion disorder
Operates outside conscious awareness

right.title: Secondary Gain
points: Tangible external real-world benefits
Exemption from work and family obligations
Monetary disability and insurance claims
Consciously exploited in malingering

steps.tx: **Detection of malingering** relies on clinical suspicion aroused by marked discrepancy between claimed disability and objective findings, lack of cooperation during diagnostic evaluations, and presence of antisocial personality disorder. Specialized forced-choice psychological tests, such as the Test of Memory Malingering, reveal performance significantly worse than chance.
steps.say: Malingering is suspected when claims clash with objective exams. Specialized forced-choice testing reveals scores worse than random chance.

vis.title: Malingering Warning Indicators
rows: Referred by attorney or pending criminal trial
High index of suspicion for feigned symptoms
Claims total blindness yet avoids colliding with furniture
Direct physical evidence contradicts symptom report
Refuses standard tests or acts uncooperatively
Fear of objective detection and exposure
Scores below fifty percent on two-alternative forced-choice test
Active intent to fail; worse than pure random guessing
